title: Execute overload protection game day (Hosted): run drills, capture findings, and create follow-ups
creator: Talia Benson
body:
Context
We’re rolling out layered overload protection (admission control + circuit breakers + runtime bounded queues) to prevent cascading failure and provide deterministic customer-facing errors under load. This ticket is the execution tracker for the game day described in the plan.

Primary goals
1) Validate behavior under controlled overload: early shed at edge when possible, no queue blowups, control plane stays responsive.
2) Validate customer-facing semantics: stable 429/503 mapping, Redwood overload codes present, Retry-After guidance consistent, no ambiguous 5xx timeouts.
3) Validate observability and runbooks: oncall can identify overload vs internal failure quickly; dashboards reflect breaker state transitions, shed rate, queue depth, and p95/p99.
4) Identify tuning / product gaps before expanding canary beyond us-east.

References
- Game day plan (Confluence): sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/game-days/game-day-plan-hosted-overload-protection.json
- Runbook (Confluence): sources/confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/hosted-overload-mitigation-runbook.json
- Dashboard spec (Confluence): sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/overload-protection-dashboards.json
- Error taxonomy ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0147-overload-error-taxonomy-and-http-mapping.json
- Breaker state model ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0148-circuit-breaker-state-model-and-hysteresis.json

Owners / roles for the day
- Incident commander: Tomáš Novák (SRE)
- Comms + timeline scribe: Dev Patel (Support readiness) / Nora Ahmed (status & transparency)
- Breakers/routing support: Christine Wong, Mina Haddad, Ravi Menon
- Runtime support: Noah Patel, Lena Fischer, Samir Qureshi
- Observability support: Aisha Bello, Sergio Costa

Pre-req checklist (must be true before starting)
- Canary enablement in us-east for 1–2 models is active behind flag (ENG-4834)
- Metrics/traces emitted for admission decisions, shed reasons, breaker transitions (ENG-4829)
- Overload dashboards deployed and visible to oncall (ENG-4830)
- Runbook published with manual override steps and rollback path
- Perf-canary tool ready to generate step-function traffic and long-prompt spikes

Execution window
- Date/time: 2026-01-16 10:00–12:00 PT
- Region: us-east (primary), with one controlled regional impairment drill (routing-level) to validate fallback/no-fallback behavior
- Endpoints: /v1/chat/completions (streaming + non-streaming), /v1/embeddings (non-streaming)

Scenarios executed
Scenario A: Step-function traffic spike (baseline → 4x → 8x)
- Expected: gateway sheds first (tier-aware), breakers open for saturated (model, region, tier), runtime queues bounded, p99 degrades but does not collapse; 429/503 returned with Retry-After; no mass timeouts.

Scenario B: Long-prompt spike (prefill pressure)
- Expected: runtime shed at prefill boundary with explicit reason; prevent KV-cache thrash / memory pressure spiral; breaker signals reflect queue/memory pressure.

Scenario C: Streaming-specific overload
- Expected: consistent semantics for streaming disconnect vs normal completion; avoid half-open/close oscillation; clients see actionable error codes.

Scenario D: Partial brownout simulation (capacity signal pessimistic for one pool)
- Expected: breaker opens quickly, routing avoids pool; control plane stays responsive; no retry storm.

Pass/fail criteria (high level)
PASS if:
- p99 latency increases are bounded; no runaway queue depth; control plane error rate stays within alert-free envelope.
- Shed errors are overwhelmingly “overload-protected” (429/503) vs internal 5xx; Retry-After present on shed responses.
- Breaker transitions exhibit hysteresis (no flapping at sub-minute cadence).
- Oncall can diagnose using dashboards in <10 minutes and apply safe mitigation steps from runbook.

Data captured
- Grafana screenshots: admission rate vs shed rate, breaker state timeline, queue depth, p95/p99 latency, 429/503 by route/model
- Trace samples for each shed reason (gateway vs runtime)
- Request logs for 10 representative failures per scenario (ensure error payload contains Redwood code + request_id)

Results summary
Overall outcome: PASS with follow-ups.

What worked
- Scenario A: early shedding engaged at gateway before queue depth exceeded safe bound. Customer-visible errors were primarily 429 with Retry-After, and 503 in a smaller subset tied to routing breaker-open state.
- Scenario B: runtime shed at prefill boundary prevented memory pressure escalation; we did not observe the prior “tail-latency death spiral” pattern.
- Scenario D: control plane remained responsive; breaker-open avoided repeated attempts into the impaired pool; overall error rate increased but stayed deterministic (no timeout storm).

Issues / findings
1) Breaker half-open flapping in streaming case (Scenario C)
- Symptoms: rapid close→open transitions under bursty streaming traffic, causing error mix to alternate 429/503 within ~30–60s windows.
- Hypothesis: half-open probe volume too high for streaming requests, combined with short cool-down.
- Impact: confusing client experience and harder-to-interpret dashboard state.

2) Retry-After value inconsistency between 429 and 503
- 429 used fixed Retry-After=2s, while 503 followed breaker cool-down (observed 10–20s). This is “technically OK” but support requested clearer guidance in docs / FAQ.

3) Shed reason propagation gap for one runtime path
- For a subset of prefill sheds, we saw the gateway return generic overload code rather than the more specific runtime reason. Tracing showed missing header propagation on an internal hop.

4) Dashboard noise: label cardinality drift
- One panel broke down by “route” with high-cardinality values (full path incl. query), making it harder to read and increasing series count.

5) Runbook manual override permissions unclear
- During the drill, we paused to confirm who is authorized to apply the emergency region toggle / breaker-disable. Needs explicit callout + escalation path.

Follow-up tasks created (new tickets to be filed immediately after game day)
- ENG-4872: Adjust half-open probe policy for streaming; add guardrail to prevent close→open flapping (owner: Christine Wong)
- ENG-4873: Standardize Retry-After calculation and document rationale for 429 vs 503 (owner: Brian Murphy + Wei Chen)
- ENG-4874: Fix internal header propagation so runtime shed reasons map through to customer error payload and traces (owner: Vikram Singh)
- ENG-4875: Reduce dashboard label cardinality; align with observability standards; add “route_template” label (owner: Sergio Costa)
- ENG-4876: Update runbook with explicit permissions + emergency toggle steps; add decision tree for “overload-protected vs internal error” (owner: Owen Phillips)

Artifacts
- Timeline + notes: attached in internal doc (linked in comments)
- Screenshots: posted in #eng-sre and #incidents threads for the day

Close criteria
- Follow-up tasks filed with owners and priorities
- Game day notes linked here
- Rollout (ENG-4834) cannot expand until flapping + propagation issues are addressed or explicitly waived by SRE lead

2026-01-16 12:18 PT (Tomáš Novák): Game day complete. Overall pass; found breaker flapping under streaming (half-open probes) + one missing reason propagation path. Filing follow-ups now; will paste keys once created.
2026-01-16 16:02 PT (Tomáš Novák): Follow-ups filed: ENG-4872..ENG-4876 (see body). Notes doc linked in internal channel; adding to attachments field once final.

2026-01-17 11:30 PT (Rafael Mendes): Reviewed results. Agree with “PASS with follow-ups.” Do not expand canary beyond current models until ENG-4872 (flapping) is fixed or we have a clear mitigation (cool-down increase + probe cap).
